response.text:
Endpoint preservation does not preserve what NextItNet can access. Its dilated causal convolutions and residual paths require tracing exact dependency offsets, including holes, rather than only receptive-field width ([NextItNet paper](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf)). Recommended derivation: start with offsets S={0}; each convolution replaces S with ⋃ⱼ(S+j·d), j=0,…,k−1; residual additions and gated products union their branches’ dependencies. Include any sequence-dependent gate computation. Normalization over channels at each position preserves temporal support; normalization across sequence positions expands it. Audit actual normalization axes and inference behavior. Read the final nonpadding position in left-padded histories.

Recommended experiment: freeze the trained model in evaluation mode; preserve endpoint, padding, history length and candidates. Permute only accessible nonpadding positions excluding the endpoint, preserving their item multiset. Compare against unrestricted endpoint-preserving shuffles, which can exchange accessible and inaccessible content, and inaccessible-only permutations, which should leave predictions unchanged if dependency tracing is correct. Include identity and duplicate-item-swap controls; count actual token changes because nonidentity index permutations can leave repeated-item sequences unchanged. Report eligible-history counts, unchanged-draw frequency, displacement, score/rank changes and paired validation HR@10 differences. Precompute seeded permutations keyed by category, user and draw; reuse them across comparisons and report uncertainty across fixed draws. These are proposed controls, not an established NextItNet-specific protocol.

Accessible-only shuffling isolates sensitivity to positional arrangement conditional on fixed accessible content, but still creates potentially implausible histories. Compare local swaps or constrained shuffles with broader corruption. Research shows random shuffling can conflate behavioral sequence patterns with item availability ([RecSys study](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748042)); perturbation explanations also face distribution-shift problems ([NeurIPS study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.00786)). Performance degradation therefore supports arrangement sensitivity, not proof of temporal reasoning or causal preference dynamics; invariance likewise does not prove order is unused.
